title: 2024 United States Data Center Energy Usage Report
author_date: Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory / U.S. Department of Energy. December 2024; modeled 2023 operations.
scope: Water and Emission Impacts, printed pages 55–58. Historical model: 176 TWh, 66 billion liters direct consumption, 4.52 L/kWh electricity-source intensity. Not a national meter census or AI-only inventory. Exact 2028 figure endpoints are not used.

title: Spatially and Temporally Detailed Water and Carbon Footprints of U.S. Electricity Generation and Use
author_date: Siddik, Shehabi, Rao and Marston; Water Resources Research. 2024.
scope: Water IMPACT: electricity flows and source-water coefficients. Average attribution differs from the causal response to an added load; hourly electricity data do not make every water input an hourly observation.

title: Water use across the conterminous United States, water years 2010–20
author_date: U.S. Geological Survey. January 2025; observation/model period 2010–2020.
scope: DOI 10.3133/pp1894D. Modeled CONUS assessment. Different-year benchmark used for scale, not a same-year sector share.

title: Cooling Water Intakes
author_date: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Agency guidance.
scope: Intake impingement and entrainment describe a mechanism, not harm established at an unnamed facility.

title: Data Centers in Virginia: study summary
author_date: Virginia Joint Legislative Audit and Review Commission. December 2024.
scope: Then-current water sustainability assessment, differing local demands and future concerns. Not approval of every future proposal.

title: Water Reuse Case Study: Quincy, Washington
author_date: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Includes 2021 operations.
scope: Utility financing; estimated 138 million gallons/year avoided potable demand; makeup supply and 2021 canal-to-groundwater switch. Avoided potable demand is not zero evaporation. The source page’s inconsistent 2.1-billion-gallon/8-million-liter conversion is not used.

title: Cooling Water Efficiency Opportunities for Federal Data Centers
author_date: U.S. Department of Energy, FEMP. Engineering guidance.
scope: Cooling stages, WUE/PUE, blowdown and cooling alternatives. Design options are not evidence of realized performance at a named facility.

title: Sustainable by design: Next-generation datacenters consume zero water for cooling
author_date: Microsoft. December 9, 2024. Operator announcement.
scope: Staged deployment; administrative water use and electricity tradeoff. Not zero lifecycle water or proof of fleet-wide completion.

title: Clean Air Act Resources for Data Centers
author_date: U.S. Environmental Protection Agency. Agency guidance.
scope: Stationary engines, turbines and operating requirements. Actual emissions and exposure require operating data.

title: Technology Changes, but Energy Efficiency Principles Remain Steadfast in Data Center Design
author_date: U.S. Department of Energy, FEMP. Engineering guidance.
scope: Efficiency and heat recovery. Recoverable heat is not automatically measured displacement of other heating.

title: Key Questions on Energy and AI: Executive summary
author_date: International Energy Agency. 2026; estimates for 2025.
scope: Estimated global data-center electricity growth of 17% and AI-focused growth of 50%. Not an indefinitely exponential law or a new U.S. water forecast.

title: Generative AI at Work
author_date: Brynjolfsson, Li and Raymond; Quarterly Journal of Economics. 2025.
scope: Staggered deployment involving 5,172 agents. Approximately 15% higher issues resolved per hour on average, with heterogeneous effects. Not a resource-savings study or an economy-wide randomized trial.

title: A Pragmatic Randomized Controlled Trial of Ambient Artificial Intelligence to Improve Health Practitioner Well-Being
author_date: Afshar and colleagues; NEJM AI. Online November 26, 2025; December 2025 issue.
scope: 24-week stepped-wedge trial; 66 ambulatory physicians/advanced practice practitioners. Note-time reduction 0.36 hours per normalized eight hours of patient time; exhaustion/disengagement improved; professional fulfillment did not meet the co-primary threshold. No quota-change intervention or downstream patient-outcome result is established here. Full text revisited September 25, 2026.

title: Measuring the Impact of Early-2025 AI on Experienced Open-Source Developer Productivity
author_date: METR. July 10, 2025.
scope: 16 developers, 246 tasks; AI-allowed tasks took 19% longer. Access was randomized; use was not compulsory.

title: We are Changing our Developer Productivity Experiment Design
author_date: METR. February 24, 2026.
scope: Changes in tools, participation and time measurement limit direct extrapolation of the earlier result.

title: Judging LLM-as-a-Judge with MT-Bench and Chatbot Arena
author_date: Zheng and colleagues; NeurIPS 2023 Datasets and Benchmarks.
scope: Useful human-preference agreement on studied benchmarks alongside position, verbosity and self-enhancement biases. Preference agreement is not universal factual verification.

title: AI Risk Management Framework: Core
author_date: National Institute of Standards and Technology. AI RMF 1.0.
scope: Voluntary, context-sensitive testing and monitoring guidance. Not a certification of a named system or mandatory human approval of every output.

title: Estimating and Reporting Avoided Emissions
author_date: GHG Protocol. Methodological working paper.
scope: Reference scenarios and comparative impacts. Useful new capability is not automatically an avoided-resource result; productivity alone does not establish physical substitution.

title: Commissioner See’s Remarks on the Large Load Show Cause Orders, E-7 to E-12
author_date: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. June 18, 2026.
scope: Explains shared-cost responsibilities, stranded-asset risk and avoiding duplicate security where retail credit support already exists. Remarks and proceedings are not a universal retail tariff. Revisited September 25, 2026.

title: Accurate structure prediction of biomolecular interactions with AlphaFold 3
author_date: Abramson and colleagues; Nature 630, 493–500. May 8, 2024.
scope: Original research on structure/interactions prediction, with benchmark improvements and stated limitations. Not a claim that a prediction itself cures a disease or establishes sector-wide environmental benefits. Primary text consulted September 25, 2026.

title: Fact Sheet: FERC Takes Action to Supercharge America’s Grid for Efficiency, Reliability, and a Bold Energy Future
author_date: Federal Energy Regulatory Commission. June 18, 2026.
scope: Official explanation of region-specific show-cause proceedings, flexible-load service and preserved state retail/siting roles. It does not enact the article’s illustrative 50/150-MW water-performance gate. Consulted September 25, 2026.
